newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 13.

text.p: Two of Mexico's crude shipping ports were shut early Monday due to high winds, for a total of five Gulf of Mexico ports shut, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its daily report 1000 local/1600 GMT.
Pajaritos, under the jurisdiction of Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz state, was closed at 0440 local/1040 GMT Monday amid winds between 50 to 60 km per hour.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state closed at 0600 local/1200 GMT Thursday, and was expected to remain closed Friday amid winds of 40 to 50 km per hour, port captain Jorge Rojano Rodriguez said.
The largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open, although port officials said wind speeds expected to reach 60 km later in the day could shut the port.

Pajaritos ships an average 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude and Dos Bocas exports 300,000 bpd, according to the latest oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) statistics. Cayo Arcas ships an average 600,000 bpd.
Veracruz port in the state of the same name was shut along with Frontera in Tabasco and Campeche in Campeche state.
Sailing was closed to smaller boats at Tampico,Tuxpan, and Ciudad del Carmen because of high winds.
The report also warned against sailing in the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of intense winds and waves expected later in the day.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

A weak cold front headed south over the middle of the Baja California peninsula at 15 knots (28 kilometers/17 miles per hour) and lowering temperatures in the area and in the states of Sonora and Chihuahua.
Possible rains along the coast and winds from the west and southwest at 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 kilometers/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves five to seven feet high.
A stationary cold front along the northern gulf arriving in central Veracruz state and bringing moderate rains and wind gusts along northern and central gulf region.

A mass of cold air moving slowly southeast, bringing winds of 25 to 30 knots (47 to 56 km/28 to 34 miles per hour) and gusts of up to 35 knots (66 km/39 miles per hour), with waves up to 14 feet high on the coasts of Tamaulipas and Veracruz, expected to move down the shore later today.
Cloudy with light rains and gusty winds along the northwest Carribean, with winds from the east and northeast at 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/17 to 22 miles) and waves of three to five feet high.
